name: Bassari Country: Bassari, Fula and Bedik Cultural Landscapes
description: In the hills of south-east Senegal, near the Guinea border, three neighbouring peoples have shaped a landscape of terraced rice paddies, scattered hamlets and old archaeological sites. Bedik villages are tight clusters of huts with steep thatched roofs, while the Bassari and Fula have settled the surrounding valleys and slopes since the 11th century. Their living traditions are still practised today.
